title: Cyber Security posture
heading:
How strong is your
cyber security posture?
lead: Eight quick questions across the controls that stop most real-world attacks give you an instant read on where you stand and what to fix first.

items.name: Multi-factor authentication
items.q: Is MFA in place across your important accounts?
opts: On a few key accounts only.
On email, remote access, and admin accounts.

items.name: Patching & updates
items.q: How consistently are systems and software kept up to date?
opts: On a regular schedule across most systems.
Promptly and automatically, with no end-of-life software in use.

items.name: Backups
items.q: Are backups taken, kept safe, and tested?
opts: Tested restores, with an offline or immutable copy.

items.name: Endpoint protection
items.q: What protects your laptops, servers, and devices?

items.name: Security awareness
items.q: Are your people trained to spot phishing and scams?
opts: Regular training and the occasional phishing test.
Ongoing training with simulations and measured improvement.

items.name: Access & admin control
items.q: How well is access to systems and admin rights controlled?
opts: Role-based access with limited admin rights.
Least privilege, reviewed regularly and logged.

items.name: Email & web filtering
items.q: Is malicious email and web content filtered before it reaches users?
opts: Email and web filtering in place and managed.
Layered filtering with reporting and tuning.

items.name: Incident readiness
items.q: Would you know what to do in a security incident?
opts: A rough idea, nothing written down.
A tested plan with clear roles and contacts.
